articles.title: World Matchplay Darts: Cameron Menzies withdraws after becoming unwell on stage during second-round match against Ross Smith
articles.summary: Cameron Menzies was 2-1 up in the second-round match against Ross Smith when he doubled over in discomfort and appeared to become unsteady on his feet; the Scot received medical attention, with the PDC later confirming he had experienced high blood pressure
articles.body:
Menzies was 2-1 up in the second-round match when he doubled over in discomfort and appeared to become unsteady on his feet, with Smith and the match officials coming to his aid.

The 37-year-old received medical attention after being taken from the stage, with the PDC later confirming Menzies had experienced high blood pressure. After medical checks, Menzies was deemed well enough to return to his accommodation.

Menzies took to social media on Wednesday night, reassuring fans over his condition and thanking those who had wished him well.

"Thanks to everyone who's checked in and sent messages. I'm okay," he wrote on Facebook.

He later added: "Unfortunately, I wasn't well enough to continue the match. It's obviously not how I wanted my World Matchplay to end, especially after playing some of the best darts of my career over the last few weeks.

"I'm grateful to the medical team for looking after me, to Ross for checking on me, and to everyone at the Winter Gardens for their support.

"A big good luck to Ross for the rest of the tournament. I wish him all the best. Hopefully I'll be back doing what I love very soon. Thanks again for all your support, it really does mean a lot."

Menzies' enforced withdrawal saw the match officially abandoned, with Smith progressing to the quarter-finals where he will face Gerwyn Price.

A statement from the PDC said: "Cameron Menzies was taken ill during his round two match against Ross Smith at the Betfred World Matchplay on Wednesday evening.

"Cameron experienced high blood pressure, which caused him to feel dizzy and subsequently faint.

"Following an assessment by the on-site medical team, Cameron was deemed well enough to return to his accommodation.

"We wish Cameron all the best and look forward to seeing him back in action soon."

Following a short break, Gian van Veen's match against Wessel Nijman commenced.

"I echo the thoughts of everybody; right now, it's all about Cameron Menzies," Sky Sports' Glen Durrant said.

"He's in tip-top form at the moment. It's a real tough one to take."

Menzies had advanced to the second round of the World Matchplay Darts after beating 2024 champion Luke Humphries 10-7, a victory he called "the biggest moment of my darts career."

The Scot produced a Big Fish checkout to beat the world No 2, and afterwards, was left lost for words.

"I don't know how to explain that [victory]. I did believe in my heart that I could maybe cause an upset but I would have to play it out of my skin," Menzies said.

"I wouldn't say I played it out of my skin, but I played really well. I did say before the game started, to beat Luke, I need to take every chance that he gives me.

"It's not like Luke to give a lot of chances away, but obviously I'm going to take it. A lot went in. I was happy. I stole a few legs to win, but it's made the best moment of my darts career."

Who will win this year's World Matchplay Darts? Luke Littler is defending the title and you can watch all the action on Sky Sports. Stream darts and more top sport with NOW .

articles.title: "Karl Malone could be sick and having a baby at home and he will get a foul" - Dennis Rodman went to war with officials in 1994
articles.summary: One thing about Dennis Rodman, the guy never changed.
articles.body:
Dennis Rodman 's "hate affair" with the officials had been going on as long as he could remember. As a member of the "Bad Boys" of the Detroit Pistons , he learned to walk a fine line between dirty and physicality. Of course, that puts The Worm under the referees' microscope at all times.

His move to San Antonio did little to improve that relationship. If anything, it brought the animosity from both sides to an all-time high.

Rodman felt the Spurs got the short end of the stick on the refs' calls, particularly in a late-season matchup against the Utah Jazz in 1994. And then, everything spilled over when the teams met again in the first round of the postseason.

Rodman lamented how the Spurs couldn't get any calls

The 1993-94 season was a weird one for the NBA. The three-time defending champion Chicago Bulls lost their heart and soul, Michael Jordan, to retirement. As a result, many felt the title was up for grabs, along with the MVP race and spots on the All-Star and All-NBA teams.

That put David Robinson firmly in the spotlight. The Admiral was having one of the finest seasons of his career, finishing second in MVP voting while averaging 29.8 points and 11.6 rebounds, both career-highs.

But as far as Rodman was concerned, D-Rob wasn't getting the respect he deserves. He believed other established stars were receiving calls that his teammate couldn't seem to buy and one name in particular kept coming up whenever The Worm aired his grievances.

"Karl Malone could be sick and having a baby at home and he will get a foul. But when it comes to David, he can't get a foul. He goes to church. What else does he need?" Rodman reacted .

Robinson attempted 14 free throws that night, two more than the entire Jazz starting lineup (12). However, the Demolition Man noted how Robinson "doesn't get a call when it counts."

"When a team like Utah beats you, it's ridiculous. For some reason, we are like the Rodney Dangerfields of the (expletive) NBA. David Robinson doesn't get a call when it counts. He has to work his (expletive) off to get a call. I guess he's not a superstar. I guess you have to be Michael Jordan to get a foul," he continued.

At one point, The Menace took matters into his own hands. He headbutted John Stockton, which got him fined and suspended, before criticizing the referees in a media conference. The Jazz point guard downplayed the incident , but apparently, it was Dennis' way of expressing his frustration over what he felt was unfair treatment.

As one would expect out of Rodman, his complaining never stopped. The No. 4 Spurs drew the No. 5 Jazz in the '94 playoffs and went at the refs again after San Antonio lost Game 3, 72-105. Malone and Stockton were again collateral damage in Rodman's rant.

"Stockton, he holds and throws David (Robinson) down, but they look at Stockton and say, `That's OK. You're all right.' And you get Karl Malone pushing and elbowing and hitting people hard, but, `That's OK. You're a good Samaritan. You live in Utah.' Stockton's supposed to be a good Samaritan, but he's cussing at me," Rodman said .

The Spurs ultimately lost the series, 3-1.

Three years later, it's like nothing changed. Rodman, playing for the Bulls, again criticized Malone and the referees in the 1997 NBA Finals. He changed his tune a bit in 1998, especially after the officials allowed more physicality in Game 2 of the Finals rematch. But still, the latter was more of a dig than a show of gratitude.

articles.title: Jacob Markstrom Shines In Panthers Debut, Florida Opens Season With 1-0 Overtime Win At Carolina
articles.summary: Veteran netminder Jacob Markstrom delivered a defensive masterclass, stonewalling Carolina’s power play before Gus Forsling buried a dramatic buzzer-beater t...
articles.body:
A new Florida Panthers season is finally upon us.

The fun all started with Tuesday's 1-0 overtime win over the Carolina Hurricanes in the NHL's first game of the season.

Starring for the Panthers in his first game back with the franchise was veteran goaltender Jacob Markstrom .

He finished the game with 15 saves, playing a very steady role in net and not putting his defenseman in any bad spots with poor rebounds while keeping the Cats in the game long enough for Gus Forsling to find the game-winning goal with just over four seconds left in overtime.

Markstrom was also key in helping Florida's defensive-minded approach by constantly jumping out of the crease and playing the puck, cutting down Carolina entry attempts and dump-ins while also helping clear the puck out of precarious areas and blocking passes with his excellent stickwork.

In terms of stopping the puck, one particular sequence late during the second period stood out, with Carolina on the power play and pushing for the game's first goal.

As Andrei Svechnikov and Sebastian Aho drove the net, Markstrom somehow kept the puck from going in, flashing his massive leg pads while maintaining strong positioning in the goal crease.

Of Markstrom's 15 saves, four were considered high-danger shots, according to Natural Stat Trick.

He also stopped Carolina seven times during their six power play opportunities, though plenty of credit is also due to Florida's penalty killers.

On defense, Aaron Ekblad , Niko Mikkola , Seth Jones and Forsling gobbled up the majority of the shorthanded minutes, while three forward duos – Sasha Barkov and Sam Reinhart , Anton Lundell and Eetu Luostarinen , Garnet Hathaway and Lars Eller – were excellent when called upon.

With the 1-0 victory, Markstrom becomes just the third goalie in Panthers history to pick up a shutout win in a season opener, joining Roberto Luongo , who shut down the Atlanta Thrashers 2-0 to open the 2005-06 season, and Jose Theodore, who blanked the New York Islanders 2-0 to kick off Florida's playoff-bound 2011-12 campaign.

Next up for the Panthers will be another home opener, this time for the San Jose Sharks .

Puck drop from SAP Center is set for Thursday at 10 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Super League Grand Final: George Williams hoping to change course of Warrington Wolves' history with victory in his final game
articles.summary: Warrington Wolves captain George Williams is looking to leave on a high by bringing home the club's first Grand Final win; watch Warrington Wolves take on Wakefield Trinity in the Super League Grand Final on Saturday October 3, live on Sky Sports from 5pm
articles.body:
When Williams returned from the NRL in 2021, he made the bold decision to not go back to his hometown club of Wigan and instead headed to Warrington.

After five years there, he is poised to return to Australia and has one last opportunity to try and depart with a trophy.

It is set to be a pretty-evenly-matched Grand Final as third- and fourth-placed Warrington and Wakefield Trinity do battle. Two underdog teams who beat the first- and second-placed sides to make it to Old Trafford.

It is not lost on Williams how big this match is as he could lead Warrington to their maiden Grand Final triumph to become just the sixth team in the history of the competition to lift the Super League trophy.

He has tasted that glory with Wigan as a youngster and now wants to leave the Wolves with another career highlight and change the direction of the club.

"It is crucial, there are so many different narratives that you want to get the win, but personally, I was pretty vocal, I came here to change history and win with Warrington," Williams told Sky Sports .

"It is pretty fitting it is my last game and I've got the opportunity to do that. Personally, that would be brilliant, a great way to go out, but there's a lot more different narratives we have got for the club and the town to do it."

Warrington take on a Wakefield team who pulled off an almighty shock with their 33-6 victory over favourites Wigan in their own backyard.

Williams knows if Trinity turn up in that form again, Warrington will need to be on their A-game.

"We know Wakefield play a good brand of rugby, they have been posting points all year, we played them three or four weeks ago and they beat us, so we know what they're capable of," he added.

"I think everyone saw Wigan as favourites and we were surprised by that one.

"Both teams have been pretty consistent all year, third and fourth, I think that's probably the word I want to use for us this year, consistent.

"Now we've just got to bring it one more time and are 80 minutes away from history which is the biggest key for us."

How to watch the Super League Grand Final

The Super League Grand Final takes place at Old Trafford on Saturday October 3, live on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports+ .

The match will kick-off at 6pm, with coverage on Sky Sports from 5pm.

articles.title: Sports Ministry top brass to skip Asian Games, focus on BRICS Games
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The higher-ranking Sports Ministry officials, including Sports Secretary Hari Ranjan Rao, have cancelled their plans to travel to Aichi-Nagoya
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The higher-ranking Sports Ministry officials, including Sports Secretary Hari Ranjan Rao, have cancelled their plans to travel to Aichi-Nagoya for the ongoing Asian Games. It has been reliably learnt that the top brass will remain in the country to oversee the BRICS Traditional and Indigenous Sports Demonstration Games on October 12-13 in Ahmedabad.Rao, who was scheduled to fly out to Japan on September 28, altered his plans keeping the importance of the BRICS Games in mind. An official from the sports ministry denied reports that the move came because of India's underwhelming show in Japan."Secretary Sports (Rao), being the senior-most officer of the Ministry decided to monitor the preparation of the Games, given the time left for the Games to begin, which would have been difficult to do from Japan. Therefore, he has cancelled his trip to the Asian Games," a source told TimesofIndia.com.It has also been learnt that the Sports Ministry had always intended to keep the officials contingent limited as part of an austerity drive. With the closing ceremony scheduled for October 4, Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) CEO Col. NS Johal is one of the highest-ranking officials available in Aichi-Nagoya.Organisation of the BRICS Games is being coordinated between the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS), the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) and the Gujarat government. Around 2,000 athletes, officials and other participants from nine countries, including China, Russia, Iran, Bolivia, are due to attend the non-competitive tournament. The focus of the Games will be on showcasing traditional and indigenous sports and cultural practices from BRICS nations.With India due to host the Commonwealth Games in 2030 and bidding to host the 2036 Olympics, both in Ahmedabad, successful hosting of the BRICS Games has been considered as critical for the country's image as a sporting nation.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Max Verstappen reveals the one thing about fatherhood he loves most as F1 star opens up on daughter Lily
articles.summary: Max Verstappen has opened up about life as a father and revealed the part of raising his daughter Lily that means the most to him.
articles.body: Max Verstappen has opened up about life as a father and revealed the part of raising his daughter Lily that means the most to him. The four-time Formula 1 world champion spoke about fatherhood during an appearance on P1 with Matt and Tommy. Verstappen said watching Lily grow and learn new things has become one of his favourite parts of life away from the F1 paddock.The Red Bull driver has always been known for his intense focus on racing. However, becoming a father has given him a different perspective. Verstappen said having a family to return to has made him calmer and helped him understand that there is more to life than Formula 1.Max Verstappen says watching daughter Lily grow is his favourite part of fatherhoodMax Verstappen said he particularly enjoys watching Lily develop as a person. He explained that every time he returns home from an F1 weekend, she has often learned something new.He said, “Honestly, watching her grow and her calling me by my name. Every weekend when I come back home, she’s learning new things, and yes, watching her evolve as a human being, in a way you don’t want her to grow up, you want her to stay like that, but you also want to see how she grows, it’s really nice.”The moment has given Verstappen a new appreciation for the small parts of family life. He admitted there is a strange feeling that comes with watching a child grow.He wants Lily to stay young and enjoy the stage she is in. At the same time, he is excited to see the person she will become.Verstappen has previously spoken openly about wanting to become a father. He said having a daughter has been a very special experience and has changed his outlook away from the racetrack.“I always knew I wanted to have children, so having a daughter now is great. I enjoy it a lot,” Verstappen said last year. “It probably also makes you a little more calm in life, more responsible, and makes you realize there’s more to life than just Formula 1.”For a driver whose career has been built around winning, Verstappen also made it clear that family has become more important than his achievements in motorsport.“Seeing your child for the first time, like your little baby, that’s something very special. Seeing your family happy, having a good time, living a good life; for me that’s way more important than whatever we achieve in motorsport”, he added.Fatherhood has also given Verstappen experience through his relationship with Kelly Piquet and her daughter Penelope. He has been part of Penelope’s life since she was young, giving him an early experience of being a bonus dad.Despite the changes at home, Verstappen has rejected the idea that becoming a father has affected his speed or competitive mindset in F1. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian shooter Rahi Sarnobat said video footage could perhaps have helped verify what happened during her controversial zero shot at the Asian Games in Japan.Sarnobat’s campaign in the women’s 25m sports pistol event took a disappointing turn on September 28 when one of her shots was ruled to have hit the frame of the target.The decision cost her valuable points in the opening series of the Rapid round. She scored 86 out of 100 instead of the 96 she expected, which affected India’s medal chances in the event.‘I am not fully convinced’Sarnobat said she could not say whether the shot was a misfire or went off target. She added that there was no unusual sound when she fired the shot.“Frankly, I cannot say that it was a misfire or it was off target. I fired all the shots, and we can hear if the ammunition is hitting somewhere other than the target,” Sarnobat told PTI.“There was no unusual sound. So, I am not fully convinced that the shot was not on the target,” she added.‘Maybe video footage could have helped’Sarnobat said video footage might have helped settle the issue, but added that cameras are not normally used for such incidents in the 25m event.“Maybe video footage could have helped, but this is standard practice. You usually do not have cameras for these incidents. It is not that cameras were not there for the Games; it is just not the standard practice,” she said.The Indian shooter also revealed that her team tried to challenge the decision twice.“Yes, we went for a review twice. There were two reviews. Usually, it is a photograph that is produced after the incident if you raise a claim,” she said.“There are certain rules to sort that out, and after all that, they have given the result that we have today,” she added.‘25m event is quite unpredictable’Sarnobat said such incidents are not unusual in the 25m event because of its unpredictable nature.“There are certain rules because the 25m event is quite unpredictable. So many incidents happen in 25m on a daily basis. There are enough rules to minimise the possibility of wrong decisions or whatever. But sometimes, I think, things are beyond that,” she said.‘I am still unable to accept it’The shooter admitted that she was still finding it difficult to move on from the incident.“Yes, it is disappointing. I am still unable to accept it. I am aware that I have to accept it and move forward as soon as possible because there is so much to do,” she said.“There are so many competitions coming up, and there is a journey ahead,” she added.‘I need some time to process’Sarnobat said she wants to spend some time with her family before reviewing what happened and moving forward.“I need some time to process. It is not like something happened yesterday and the next day you just carry forward as if nothing happened.“I don't think that is going to be the case.“So, I will take my time. articles.title: LIV's future now down to player support - Bland
articles.summary: LIV golfer Richard Bland reveals that the future of the league will rely on "player support" with their members still left in the dark as to what will happen...
articles.body:
LIV golfer Richard Bland has said the future of the league will rely on "player support" with members still in the dark as to what will happen going forward.

In early September LIV filed for bankruptcy protection with at least $45m (£33m) owed to players.

This followed news in April that the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF) would end its multibillion dollar backing of the tour at the end of the season, leaving the future of the series in doubt.

In August, the tour announced it had secured an unnamed lead investor to keep the competition running in 2027, a proposal widely branded as 'LIV 2.0'.

Southampton-based Bland from Southampton joined in 2022 and admitted he is yet to definitively know what will happen going forward.

"The funding is all there," he told BBC South Today.

"Once everything does get sorted out with LIV 1.0 it's then down to player support and who is going to sign up for the new league.

"Even though the funding is there, theoretically there's no guarantee that LIV 2.0 will continue if they don't have the player support."

Since entering the sport in 2021, LIV has signed some of the biggest names in golf, with Bryson Dechambeau and John Rahm among the notable figures to leave the PGA Tour for the lucrative venture.

According to Bland, a meeting took place at the start of the year where players were told that tour would be financially backed for the next six years.

But in April around an event in Mexico, reports started to emerge that this would not be the case as PIF governor Yasir Al-Rumayyan stepped down from the board.

"We were told in Riyadh in around late January that the league was going to be funded through to 2032," Bland added.

"That was from Yasir as well, so from the horse's mouth so to speak.

"Everyone came away from that player meeting really positive and excited for the future, then four months later in Mexico to find out that the tour was going to get wrapped up, a lot of guys couldn't believe it.

"It's very sad and it's been a very difficult journey to navigate, more so for staff and Scott [O'Neil, LIV CEO] to forge a pathway forward, we're still a bit in the dark with how it's going to be going forward."

Bland became the oldest first-time winner in European Tour history when he won the British Masters at the Belfry in 2021.

The now 53-year-old also claimed the 2024 Senior PGA Championship in what was his first start in a senior event.

Throughout his time on LIV, Bland admitted that reports he had earned over $20m while on the tour were "somewhere in the right ballpark".

He was one of the first to join the tour and featured in their first event which took place in London, going on to represent Martin Kaymer's Cleeks GC.

"At 49 years old, when the opportunity came along, you would have been mad to not take it," he added.

"I was living comfortably on DP World but I was given the chance to play for seven to eight times more money, some people won't agree with that and that's absolutely fine.

"That decision was mine and one that I made for my family and my security going forward, in my eyes it was a no-brainer.

"I'm now in the fortunate position now where if LIV 2.0 doesn't come about then it doesn't affect me as much as it probably does some of the younger players."

With the future of LIV golf still uncertain, some of the stars of the league have recently been competing in DP World Tour events in Europe.

John Rahm, Joaquin Niemann and Tyrrell Hatton were at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth two weeks ago, also competing in the Irish Open the week prior.

Bland will continue that trend as he makes his first DP World Tour start since 2023 on Thursday in the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship in Scotland.

articles.title: Is Frances Tiafoe the Perfect Man to Send Off Kei Nishikori?
articles.summary: To be fair to the legendary Kei Nishikori, he could have drawn considerably easier opponents for what may become the final match of his professional career....
articles.body:
To be fair to the legendary Kei Nishikori , he could have drawn considerably easier opponents for what may become the final match of his professional career. However, there may not be many better ones. Nishikori will begin his final Japan Open against Frances Tiafoe, the No. 2 seed and current No. 8 in the world .

The Japanese star has already confirmed that Tokyo will be his final tournament before retirement, meaning a first-round defeat would end one of the most important careers in Asian tennis history. From a purely competitive perspective, it is a brutal draw. From almost every other perspective though, Tiafoe feels strangely perfect for the occasion.

Is Tiafoe the Perfect Man to Send Nishikori Off?

Tiafoe Will Understand Exactly What This Match Is

Some players could walk into Ariake Coliseum, put their headphones on, treat the evening like another first round, and leave the emotional stuff for everybody else. Not this guy. Tiafoe has never been that kind of guy.

The American has built much of his own identity around crowds and occasions. The ATP has described him as one of the tour's great performers, somebody whose personality and tennis tend to expand when an arena becomes louder. His relationship with the US Open crowd has become particularly famous, and Tiafoe himself has repeatedly spoken about feeding off that energy.

Tokyo should provide plenty of it. Nishikori is far from simply a retiring veteran receiving a wild card at his home tournament. He is the most successful Japanese men's player of the Open Era, a former No. 4, a 12-time ATP Tour champion and the first Asian man to reach a Grand Slam singles final.

He also has history at this particular tournament. Nishikori won Tokyo in 2012 and 2014, finished runner-up in 2018, and owns a 24-9 record at the event. It's no coincidence he's deciding to end it here. Tiafoe will understand that.

Back in July, months before the draw, he was asked about Nishikori's retirement. Tiafoe spoke warmly about him, calling himself a big fan and describing Nishikori as one of the nicest players around. He also joked that he hoped they would meet before the end because Nishikori had beaten him in their only previous match and he wanted another chance before the Japanese star disappeared.

The draw apparently listened. They last met in Vienna in 2018, when Nishikori won 7-6 5-7 6-2. Eight years later, they get one more.

It Should Still Feel Like a Proper Tennis Match

That might actually be the nicest part of this pairing. Tiafoe is not arriving as some ceremonial opponent. In many ways, he is playing arguably the best tennis of his career. The 28-year-old reached the Cincinnati final before making another deep run at the US Open, where he reached the semi-finals for the third time. That stretch helped take him to a career-high No. 8.

So if this is the end for Nishikori, it will not be because somebody gently escorted him towards retirement. He will have to play a top-ten opponent who wants to beat him, and that matters.

Sometimes there's something slightly uncomfortable about farewell matches when the occasion overwhelms the competition itself. The crowd wants one outcome, everybody knows what the evening represents, and the actual tennis begins to feel secondary.

Tiafoe is almost uniquely equipped to avoid that. He will play, and he will compete, but he won't diminish the occasion in any way because that's just who he is as a player. And if the atmosphere becomes emotional, he is unlikely to spend the evening pretending not to notice it.

There is room for both. Nishikori deserves a serious opponent in his final tournament. He also deserves someone who can recognize that thousands of people inside the stadium are not simply watching a first-round ATP 500 match. They may be saying goodbye.

Tiafoe understands theatre better than most tennis players, without usually letting the theatre replace the tennis. That should come in handy.

Of course, Nishikori may ruin the entire farewell narrative by winning. That would be pretty funny but in some ways also fitting. His career has contained enough comebacks from injuries and enough stubborn deciding-set victories that one more would hardly feel inappropriate.

Even at 36, even with his ranking down after years of physical problems, a part of the Tokyo crowd will hope the goodbye can be postponed for another round. Tiafoe will be trying to prevent that, and he should.

He knows what Nishikori has meant to Japanese tennis. He knows this could be the final match. He likes big crowds, embraces unusual occasions and appears genuinely fond of the man standing across the net.

He is also No. 8 in the world and good enough to make sure Nishikori has to produce something special if he wants another night. Maybe that is about as appropriate as a final opponent can be. If Nishikori wins, Tokyo gets to celebrate him once more. If he loses, Frances Tiafoe seems like exactly the sort of person who will know when the match has stopped being about him.

articles.title: Giants Issued Clear J.J. McCarthy Outlook After Trade With Vikings
articles.summary: Former Minnesota Vikings QB J.J. McCarthy will be looking for a fresh start with the New York Giants after the trade on Sept. 28. Minnesota received a 2027 f...
articles.body:
Former Minnesota Vikings QB J.J. McCarthy will be looking for a fresh start with the New York Giants after the trade on Sept. 28.

Minnesota received a 2027 fifth-round pick in exchange for McCarthy, and now the question will be whether the former first-round pick sees the field in New York this season. Nonetheless, several variables could make that happen.

One is that Jameis Winston keeps playing at a subpar level, which he has done through two games after taking over for starting QB Jaxson Dart , who is out for the rest of the season. The other is how long it will take for McCarthy to learn the Giants' offense.

NFL insider James Palmer shared his outlook on when McCarthy could be ready to see the field for New York; now that doesn't mean he will.

"When does he play? That's one of the things that everybody's very curious about," Palmer said in a Sept. 29 video from his X account . "He's arriving, taking that physical, most likely on the practice field for the first time [on Sept. 30], and then he'll start learning this offense.

"I'm describing some characteristics of it that are similar to the strengths that J.J. McCarthy has. So he will start to get his feet wet. The last thing you want to do is just throw him out there without learning and understanding everything.

"… I would say he'll be ready Week 7, Week 8, Week 9. If Jameis Winston is playing really, really well, you're not going to make the switch. I think the timeline for this is really down to just two things. It's how quickly J.J. McCarthy picks all of this up, and it's how Jameis Winston is playing."

J.J. McCarthy Made Sense for the Giants for Style Perspective

Moreover, in the same video, Palmer said one reason McCarthy made sense for the Giants is that the former Vikings QB is mobile and New York's offense is designed for a mobile QB, since that's one of Dart's strengths.

"The other part is playing style," Palmer added. "That played a big part because Matt Nagy and that entire offensive staff spent the entire offseason coming into town with John Harbaugh and putting into place an offense that was designed around a quarterback who is mobile, a quarterback who can use his legs, a quarterback who can kind of throw on the move.

"Those are things that Jaxson Dart was great at, and those are things that J.J. McCarthy can do as well. That's why you see oftentimes there are a lot of similarities in some buildings between the backup and the quarterback's strengths in this."

Former Vikings QB Could Be Big Insurance for New York

If McCarthy plays this season and shows more of the positives he had in Minnesota than the negatives, the Giants will have major insurance behind Dart, given that their starter has had injuries in his first two seasons in the NFL.

"Then you have to protect yourself in the short term and maybe even beyond that with a move like getting a quarterback like McCarthy, who has upside and talent to be picked at the top of the draft," Palmer said. "Jaxson Dart has missed 17 of a possible 34 games in his career. You need to protect yourself moving forward as well."

articles.title: NFL Injury Update: When's Zach Charbonnet Returning To Seahawks Practice?
articles.summary: Charbonnet is recovering from an ACL injury, and is edging closer to returning to the practice field.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks' run game was always going to be a close watch this season, with no Kenneth Walker and Zach Charbonnet dealing with an ACL injury.

And after Seattle's 33-31 loss to the Washington Commanders , some are wondering how Charbonnet's recovery is going.

There was a thought that maybe he could return to the practice field this week, which would be a huge boost to the Seahawks. Granted, he's still a few months away from returning to play.

With the Seahawks' ground game struggling in Washington, Charbonnet continues to work on his rehab in the background.

But when could we see him return to the practice field?

"Yeah, no update," Macdonald said . "So, we're still working through that process. I'm sure we'll have an answer by sometime tomorrow whether or not he'll start practicing this week. So, it's not out of the question yet. We just haven't had an update."

In truth, the Seahawks won't be pushing Charbonnet at this point in his recovery, as the running back room still has plenty of bodies, and he's likely still a few months away at the very least.

But ticking off certain things on his checklist is what it is all about for Charbonnet, and returning to practice is likely a big one.

We don't know when that will be, but there is no doubt it is coming soon. Since the Seahawks are already close to having an answer on whether he can return, that tells us it will be sooner rather than later.

Until he does return, it will be Jadarian Price, Emanuel Wilson , and George Holani who will be tasked with giving Sam Darnold some help, and while they were bottled up against Washington in the previous two games, the Seahawks got some good burn on the ground.

And I'd imagine that when Charbonnet does return, that will only increase.

articles.title: Did Caitlin Clark really vomit at halftime vs. Aces?
articles.summary: Clark gave it her all to lead the Fever to a Game 2 win over the Aces
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark left it all on the court in Game 2 of the Indiana Fever 's first-round playoff series against the Las Vegas Aces . Literally.

The dynamic guard revealed after the Fever's 99-89 win that she vomited in a trash can at halftime. Clark says it was a result of sheer effort rather than sickness, so she jokingly doubled down on vomiting again during Game 3.

"Your back's up against the wall," Clark said . "You only have one more opportunity. Get ready to dominate and give it everything you can. To be honest, I threw up everything in my stomach at halftime. I was just out there so tired. It's not because I didn't feel good or anything; I was just that gassed.

"Let's throw up again at halftime of the next game. Just means you're working hard and leave it all out there. You're only guaranteed another 40 minutes, so just really proud of this group."

Clark tallied 27 points, 15 assists and seven rebounds to help stave off an Aces team that got great performances out of A'ja Wilson and Jackie Young . Now, both teams' seasons are on the line with Game 3 looming.

The winner-take-all Game 3 is set for Thursday at 9 p.m. ET in Las Vegas .

articles.title: Stephen A. Smith was ready to ‘beg’ LeBron James to join New York Knicks
articles.summary: Despite their issues, Stephen A. Smith was willing to do whatever it took to help bring LeBron James to the New York Knicks.
articles.body:
Despite their issues, Stephen A. Smith was willing to do whatever it took to help bring LeBron James to the New York Knicks .

James recently revealed that he almost joined the Knicks this summer, but opted against it after they won the NBA championship.

This revelation has prompted Smith to make a statement of his own – one that few would have expected from the ESPN figure.

Stephen A. Smith wanted LeBron James to join the Knicks if they didn't win the championship

Speaking on his show, Stephen A. Smith admitted that he was willing to do whatever it took to bring LeBron James to the New York Knicks.

While he caveated his statement by saying that it was under the condition that the Knicks didn't win the championship, Smith was ready to beg James to join his beloved team.

"Let me say this. We all know some of the history that involves yours truly and LeBron James. We do not get along. We do not talk. The history is what it is.

"It obviously existed before the New York Knicks won the championship. The fact that he's not coming to New York doesn't bother me one bit.

"But I'm going to confess to you that it is only because the New York Knicks won the championship. I am grown-a** man. There's too much love in the world to be focused on dislike and hatred. I do not hate or dislike that man. I'm over whatever it is that we got going on…

"If the New York Knicks had lost in the playoffs or in the NBA finals this year, I had every intention of begging LeBron James to come to New York. I don't give a d*** what it took. You need me to send some flowers? Need me to caddy for you while you try to play golf? What you need, bro?…

"Even in his 24th season, even approaching age 42, the brother is still one of the top 20 players in the world. His basketball IQ is unmatched. He's a four-time champion and four-time league MVP.

"To me, if the New York Knicks had not won, he would have been the clear and obvious missing link for the New York Knicks.

"And if that required some begging on my part, in order to do it, I would have done it. I would have begged LeBron James. I ain't got no shame."

Considering the history between the two figures, it's surprising to see Smith admit how much he was willing to do to help bring LeBron James to New York.

The two have been at odds since the start of 2025, when Smith made seemingly disparaging remarks about LeBron as a father.

Regardless, we'll never know what Smith would have done to convince LeBron to join the Knicks, as the franchise won their first NBA championship in 53 years.

articles.title: How They Fared: WSU's Daiyan Henley, Idaho's Kaden Elliss lead the local NFL products in Week 3

articles.body:
Sep. 30—Former Washington State linebacker Daiyan Henley always finds a way to be near the top of the Los Angeles Chargers ' tackle leaders, but this week, he did so along with a forced turnover and a pair of fumble recoveries. As for Idaho graduate Kaden Elliss , he has been the anchor of the New Orleans Saints ' defense through three weeks and leads the team in tackles on the season.

Here's how all the former Washington State Cougs, Idaho Vandals and one Moscow High alum fared in Week 3 of the 2026-27 NFL season this week:

OL, Abraham Lucas , Seattle Seahawks : Lucas started at right tackle in the Seahawks' 33-31 loss to the Commanders. Seattle QB Sam Darnold passed for 379 yards and four touchdowns, but the Seahawks mustered just 44 rushing yards as a team.

LB, Daiyan Henley, Los Angeles Chargers: The team captain recorded nine tackles (five solo), forced a fumble and recovered two fumbles in the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Bills. Henley is up to 20 tackles on the season, second on the team, only trailing former all-pro Derwin James .

QB, Gardner Minshew , Arizona Cardinals : Minshew did not play in the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers .

S, Jaden Hicks , Kansas City Chiefs : Hicks, seemingly now a full-time starter at safety, recorded seven tackles (one solo) and a pass defensed in the Chiefs' 24-10 win over the Dolphins.

LB, Frankie Luvu , Washington Commanders : Luvu did not play in the Commanders' 33-31 win over the Seahawks. Luvu missed last week against the Cowboys with a groin injury and that same ailment kept him out Sunday.

OL, Esa Pole , Washington Commanders: Pole remains on the Commanders' practice squad and did not play in the 33-31 win over the Seahawks.

CB, Chau Smith-Wade , Carolina Panthers : Smith-Wade recorded one tackle in his 15 snaps of special teams in the Panthers' 21-18 loss to the Browns.

LB, Brennan Jackson , Las Vegas Raiders : Jackson remains on injured reserve.

CB, Cam Lampkin , Los Angeles Rams : Lampkin did not play in the Rams' 30-26 loss to the Broncos on Sunday Night Football. Lampkin remains on the Rams' practice squad.

DB, Tucker Large, Philadelphia Eagles : Large remains on injured reserve.

S, Jalen Thompson , Dallas Cowboys : Thompson recorded three tackles (two solo) in the Cowboys' 34-31 loss to the Ravens .

CB, Jaylen Watson , Los Angeles Rams: Watson left the game with an injury coach Sean McVay said is a dislocated shoulder. Before he left, he recorded two tackles in the Rams' 30-26 loss to the Broncos on Sunday Night Football.

WR, Kyle Williams , New England Patriots : Williams returned five kicks for 105 yards and caught one pass for 34 yards in the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jaguars . Williams caught the pass on the sideline and used his speed to turn up field, even making it to the end zone. But the officials found his foot went out on the sideline.

QB, Cam Ward ( Miami ), Tennessee Titans : Ward completed 23-of-36 passes for 181 yards with one touchdown and an interception in the Titans' 12-7 loss to the Giants. Ward had a chance at the win, down by five with 24 seconds left inside the Giants' 10-yard line. But on first-and-goal, Ward looked right, then scrambled left and tried to loft a pass to his receiver Elic Ayomanor , but he did not put enough air on it and a Giants' defender intercepted it.

LB, Kaden Elliss, New Orleans Saints: Elliss led the Saints in tackles with nine (four solo) in New Orleans' 35-27 loss to the Raiders. Elliss' efforts up front helped the Saints limit lead back Ashton Jeanty of Boise State fame to just 2.9 yards per carry. After Sunday, Elliss now leads the Saints in tackles on the season with 24.

LB, Christian Elliss , New England Patriots: Christian Elliss recorded three tackles in his start at linebacker in the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jaguars.

LS, Hogan Hatten , Detroit Lions : Hatten recorded seven snaps at long snapper in the Lions' 31-24 win over the Jets .

CB, Marcus Harris (Cal), Tennessee Titans: Harris recorded six tackles (four solo) and two tackles for loss in the Titans' 12-7 loss to the Giants.

LB, Jonah Elliss , Denver Broncos : Jonah Elliss recorded three tackles in his start at linebacker in the Broncos' 30-26 win over the Rams on Sunday Night Football.

articles.title: Broncos WR Pat Bryant: I felt a nudge, sold enough to get the pass interference call
articles.summary: The accuracy of the pass interference call that set the Broncos up for the winning touchdown over the Rams in last Sunday night's game has been debated aroun...
articles.body:
The accuracy of the pass interference call that set the Broncos up for the winning touchdown over the Rams in last Sunday night's game has been debated around the football world, but what's not in debate is that Broncos wideout Pat Bryant did all he could to ensure a flag was thrown.

Rams defensive back Josh Wallace was covering Bryant on a pass to the sideline and Bryant did his best impression of a soccer player when he felt contact from Wallace on his back. During an interview with Romi Bean of CBS News Colorado, Bryant acknowledged that he flopped because there was a much better chance of getting a penalty than a catch on the play.

"It was a little pass interference. I did sell it just enough to get the flag," Bryant said. "He definitely gave me a little nudge that I felt. I felt like I couldn't get the ball, so it was either the ball or the call. . . . It's something that a lot of people do in this league, I kinda used it to my advantage."

It was a well-timed and well-executed move by Bryant that paid off handsomely when quarterback Bo Nix got into the end zone for the game-winning score a few plays later.

articles.title: Stearns Admits Mets Mistakes After Disappointing 2026 Season
articles.summary: David Stearns owns the Mets' failures, citing an "uncapped downside" and poor first-base play. The GM faces a tough road to fix the roster.
articles.body:
David Stearns finally stopped dancing around the hard truth. The Mets president of baseball operations admitted his own decisions created a "potential for almost an uncapped downside scenario," according to Amazin' Avenue . That is a rare moment of honesty for a front office that has spent big while producing small results. Despite enormous spending and elevated expectations, the NL East division saw the team end in last place. Stearns knows the fans are angry, and he knows he cannot blame bad luck forever.

The biggest mistake was letting Pete Alonso walk without a real replacement. Stearns told reporters that "the totality of our production at first base wasn't good enough." Alonso went to the Orioles and had a career year right in front of the Mets. Meanwhile, New York struggled to find anyone who could hit consistently at that position. Stearns said he does not get "mulligans" in this job, which means he must fix this hole before the next season starts. The team needs better success at first base for the entire year, not just a few weeks.

The roster lacked the flexibility to handle these early failures. When Juan Soto and Francisco Lindor got hurt, the team had no way to adjust. Stearns noted that "we had different elements of our roster that didn't have enough flexibility." This made it very hard to make changes once the season was already going wrong. The 12-game losing streak in April was just the start of a long nightmare. Injuries to key stars combined with poor depth created a mess that no one could fix in June.

There was some good news late in the year, but it came too late for the standings. The Mets went 34-31 after the All-Star break, a sign that the team could still play. Stearns pointed to the "real foundation here for the level of success and competitiveness that we expect to have." Young players like Carson Benge and A.J. Ewing showed promise, and Andy Green helped bring a new identity to the clubhouse. But a good September does not erase a bad May or a missing playoff berth for the second straight year.

Bo Bichette also offered a different perspective on the dark season. According to Newsday , the third baseman stated he is concentrating on ensuring the organization and team are positioned for improvement next season. He admitted the first few months were not fun, but he found growth in the struggle. Bichette has a player opt-out after this season, yet he seems willing to stay if the front office makes the right moves. His contract includes a hefty signing bonus, but the $42 million owed next year makes him a key piece to keep.

The path forward is clear but difficult. Stearns must add starting pitching depth, which was the main reason the season went haywire. He needs two rotation cogs to fix the hole left by the lack of depth. The front office has a plan, but the fans have seen plans before. The only thing that matters now is winning games. Stearns said his job is to "put a winning team on the field every year." That promise is now on thin ice.

articles.title: Yankees 'superstar' Ben Rice singlehandedly outhits Red Sox in WC win
articles.summary: Ben Rice raked four hits, including two homers, while pitcher Cam Schlittler dominated in a New York Yankees wild card win over the Boston Red Sox.
articles.body:
Sept. 30 (UPI) -- Ben Rice raked four hits, including two homers, while pitcher Cam Schlittler dominated in a New York Yankees shutout of the Boston Red Sox in Game 1 of an American League wild card series.

Schlittler allowed just two hits over 6 1/3 scoreless innings en route to the 9-0 triumph in Game 1 of the best-of-three series Tuesday at Yankee Stadium.

"I'll remember getting a W versus the Red Sox. There is nothing better than that," Rice told reporters. "I'll remember Cam going out there and just being lights out, like he always is. I'll remember that atmosphere.

"Just an awesome night and a great way to kick off the series."

Rice, a first-time All-Star this season, went 4 for 5 with six RBIs.

"I think he's just a superstar," Yankees second baseman Anthony Volpe said of Rice. "Obviously, the way the year has went with injuries and everything, I think he has carried us a lot.

The Yankees jumped on their rivals with an RBI single from catcher Austin Wells in the second inning and never looked back. Schlittler allowed a single to Red Sox catcher Adley Rutschman in the game's second at-bat, but went on to retire the next 13 batters in order.

The Yankees starter, who didn't allow another hit until the seventh inning, leaned on his curveball, while also revving in several fastballs eclipsing 100 mph in the 117-pitch effort. He threw 77 of those pitches for strikes, leading to 10 strikeouts. He issued just one walk.

"I think the natural adrenaline, just the environment and how loud it was definitely helped," Schlittler said. "Just being able to lean on that."

Rice ripped a 423-foot solo homer of relief pitcher Erik Miller in the fifth. He plated outfielder Spencer Jones with an RBI single in the seventh for a 3-0 Yankees lead.

Wells scored the fourth Yankees run when pinch hitter Luis Garcia Jr. grounded into a double play later in the inning. Wells scored shortstop George Lombard Jr. off a sacrifice fly in the eighth.

Rice brought in the Yankees' final four runs two at-bats later, when he hammered a 408-foot grand slam off relief pitcher Brayan Bello . That blast traveled 108.6 mph off the designated hitter's bat before finding the Yankees bullpen.

"Pretty remarkable," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "For [Rice and Schlittler] to go out and have that kind of night together to start this postseason, it's pretty amazing and kind of hard to grasp a little bit, frankly. But I'm certainly glad we have those two."

Yankees relief pitchers Paul Blackburn and John Schreiber combined to allow just one hit over the final 2 2/3 innings of the shutout. Lombardi went 3 for 4 with two runs scored. Wells went 2 for 3 with two RBI and a run scored.

Red Sox starter Payton Tolle allowed five hits and a run over 4 2/3 innings. No Red Sox players reached base more than once in the lopsided loss. The Red Sox Nos. 1 through 4 hitters combined to go 1 for 12 with eight strikeouts.

The Yankees (1-0) will host the Red Sox (0-1) in Game 2.

articles.title: Alex Eala eyeing LA Olympics if she takes tennis gold at the Asian Games
articles.summary: Alex Eala is closing in on two goals.  The tennis gold medalist at the Asian Games gets an automatic berth into the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.  The Philippin...
articles.body:
NAGOYA, Japan (AP) — Alex Eala is closing in on two goals.

The tennis gold medalist at the Asian Games gets an automatic berth into the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics . A two-for-one deal.

The Philippines' Eala reached the semifinals on Wednesday after defeating Joanna Garland of Taiwan 7-5, 6-0. Eala will next face Wang Xiyu of China on Thursday. The winner advances to Friday's final.

"The Olympics is a dream for me to be able to compete there, to represent my country," Eala said. "So, yeah, let's see how it goes."

She took bronze medals in singles and mixed doubles with Francis Alcantara at the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou, China, and is a favorite for gold this time.

In order to compete in the Asian Games, Eala had to withdraw from the China Open in Beijing — a mandatory WTA 1000 event. She could be fined $10,000.

She said she's not aware of any official notice from the WTA.

"I want to say that it's easy for people to relate to wanting to represent their country and wanting to play these types of Olympic Games," Eala said. She indicated other players have recognized the conflict and supported her.

One seems to be Zhang Shuai of China, No. 57 on the WTA rankings. Eala is No. 18.

"It is incredible that the two competitions are in the same weeks," Zhang said. "Some of the previous competitions have been like this. Last week, the Billie Jean King Cup was in the same week as the Singapore and Seoul competitions.

"That's life," Zhang added. "If two things are very important to you, or if they're both very important tournaments, you can choose one of them."

SNTV video journalist Nicky Zhu contributed to this report.

articles.title: 'Unrealistic to win gold every single time': Captain Srinath Narayanan after India's Chess Olympiad silver | Exclusive
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: \"Don't blame me for keeping the board order in suspense.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: "Don't blame me for keeping the board order in suspense. I had it on chess-results right from September 1." The message, though posted with a laughing emoji from Srinath Narayanan's own social media handle the moment India's board order for the 46th Chess Olympiad became public, was the first sign of how closely one particular decision was being watched.In the weeks before the team left for Samarkand, no topic dominated chess circles more than the absence of world champion Dommaraju Gukesh from the top three boards.Olympiad boards are assigned by strength, and as reigning world champion, Gukesh had always been the default choice for Board 1, exactly where he sat during India's gold-clinching Budapest campaign in 2024.But this time, a run of poor results had dropped his rating to the point where he was, remarkably, only the second-lowest-rated player in India's own squad, ahead of Vidit Gujrathi. When the board order finally went public, Gukesh was at four.Earlier this week. India came home with silver, one place below the gold they'd earned two years earlier.Sitting down with TimesofIndia.com after the tournament, captain and coach Srinath Narayanan walked through the decision that defined the build-up, the flashpoints that decided the campaign, and why he isn't interested in calling this a missed gold.How Gukesh's board four was securedThe decision itself, Narayanan acknowledged, was never made lightly."It was a difficult decision. I thought about it for a really long time. I consulted a few people, like Harikrishna (India's 87th Grandmaster), who I look up to, and also my assistant coaches," he recalled. "I spoke to all the different players, and I also deliberated over it for a few weeks before arriving at a final decision."The clearest signal came from an unlikely source, the Chennai Grand Masters tournament earlier in the year."That was where Arjun (Erigaisi), Nihal (Sarin), and Gukesh all were playing (in that tournament)," Narayanan explained. "Arjun completely belonged there and was fighting for first place. Nihal also showed pretty good chess."Gukesh, by contrast, struggled, finishing last on his home soil."The Chennai field was pretty strong, similar to what you'd face on board two, not quite board one, everyone around 2700. It was a high-pressure board, and whilst Gukesh showed some signs of playing really good chess, overall he had a very difficult time. I was hoping that would be the tournament where Gukesh gets his form back, because Chennai was what helped him get to the Candidates in 2024. But it was not to be," he added.Explaining the scenario further, the Grandmaster compared the process to physical rehabilitation. "When someone is going through a bad form like this, they are mentally recuperating, almost like how you come back from a physical injury. You can't immediately start physically exerting yourself with the most challenging physical tasks; you have to build towards it. Similarly, mentally, Gukesh had to build towards that."In Samarkand, Gukesh went on to play ten games, drawing two and winning seven before going on to lose the final round game against Hungary's Gleb Dudin.Looking ahead to SindarovWith Gukesh due to defend his world title against challenger Javokhir Sindarov later this year, the Olympiad's biggest subplot was always going to be what it meant for that match.Despite the loss in the final round, Gukesh won the silver medal on Board 4. Narayanan sees it as reason for optimism."I think Gukesh is in a much better mental space after the Olympiad, because it was probably his first really good tournament in a long time," Narayanan added."It will be close, not as one-sided as what the ratings reflect. Javokhir enters with a lot of confidence, and that can change if there's an early good result for Gukesh. He's also showing an incredible amount of opening preparation against other opponents, but in a (World Championship) match, this gets neutralised."Both players see everything the other has. There are factors going Javokhir's way right now, but they can even out over a match. I think it's going to be a very close, very interesting one."Life inside the campWhen the conversation turns from Gukesh to the silver-winning campaign, there was the simple question of what the weeks in Samarkand actually felt like from the inside."The experience was great. Just being part of such a unit, we feel quite privileged," Narayanan said with a smile. "Every player is a lot of fun, and everyone genuinely cares so much about each other. This is a team which we have had for a lot of members since 2022. There is a lot of trust and mutual belief in each other."Describing how hectic the schedule was, Narayanan continued, "There was a lot more game time and preparation time involved. We played for around five hours every day, and prepared for close to four hours."But in the free time that we got, we played outdoor sports like padel. There is a padel court within the hotel complex, which was very convenient. We also went for team walks together."The board-to-board picturePraggnanandhaa, who stepped up to lead the team on Board 1 and won an individual bronze, drew more praise from his captain than his scoresheet alone suggested."His score (6.5/10) still didn't completely reflect the level at which he played. He created chances in almost every game, quite a few draws which could have been wins. But the quality of his play was really high. It never looked like Pragg was in danger of losing. Even the couple of times he fought into slightly worse positions, body-language-wise, he was the one pushing. His opponents were the ones who were a bit stressed," the Indian coach remaked.Erigaisi's tournament was really two tournaments in one. He (5.5/10) started off with a loss and ended being the saviour for the Indian team."The first two rounds were quite unsteady for him. If we take those out, both his results and his play were at a pretty high level," Srinath told this website."There were a few simple conversions, like against Uzbekistan B, where if he had won, his score would have been much better. Against Germany, he was the one pushing, trying very hard, but couldn't quite get the win. So it was frustrating in terms of results, but in terms of the quality of his play, he showed he belongs at the highest level."Nihal Sarin's tournament carried the most consequence for the team's overall trajectory, for better and worse.His round-two win against Indonesia, Narayanan pointed out, was what put India on a collision course with Uzbekistan in the first place."We got to play Uzbekistan in round six because of Nihal's win in round two against Indonesia. He was the sole winner," the Chennai-based grandmaster added.That same player was then at the centre of the tournament's most painful moment.The challenges and how the team got through themThe real test arrived in round six, when Nihal blundered his queen in a winning position against Nodirbek Yakubboev, a loss Narayanan doesn't shy away from calling decisive."That game decided both the match and the tournament. It was probably like the final before the finals, because it was pretty clear it was going to be either Uzbekistan or India. Uzbekistan had the momentum on their side. A win against them would have changed it completely," Srinath said bluntly.What got the team through it, he said, was routine rather than any grand intervention."It really helped to have a united team spirit, supporting each other. Everyone was there for Nihal that day. It also helped to have a rest day on the very next day, we could recuperate together, spend some time playing different games, and playing something outdoor really helped."Those rituals, Narayanan explained, predate this tournament entirely as he continued, "We had a team walk ritual and a team eating ritual that we do no matter what, and a man-of-the-match ritual during team meetings. All these we established in the 2024 Olympiad. Having these routines helps face both the positives and negatives, because it brings us all together, and someone can really help someone going through a tough time. The next day, Nihal had a good sleep, because there was no game."Two more moments stayed with the captain."The eighth-round draw of Gukesh against Mahammad Muradli. He (Gukesh) had a very big advantage (against Azerbaijan), and Uzbekistan had lost their match. We saw a window of opportunity, and Gukesh missing that win felt very painful," Srinath recalled.And then the final round. "It was clear within the first 90 minutes that Gukesh's position was bad. The only other board where we could strike was Arjun's, but Gukesh's had a more winning position than Arjun's, in my opinion. So that was also pivotal."Every success story possesses challenges. And thus, Narayanan won't let those moments define the story."In hindsight, even if both results had gone our way, it's unlikely it would have changed the standings, we'd have tied with Uzbekistan and had a worse tiebreak," he told TimesofIndia.com.Silver won, or gold missed?It's the question that will follow this campaign around, and Narayanan has clearly thought about his answer."It's really important to realise that we have won silver rather than missing gold, because it's unrealistic to win gold every single time. There is no rational reason to have that kind of expectation. There are other teams who are incredibly strong, investing and practising the same way as us. Between these teams, it's roughly 50-50. Uzbekistan is one such team, who have invested heavily, and their players are top professionals, motivated, and the same age group as us," Srinath added."We didn't come to this Olympiad in the best of form. Our players were probably at their peak around 2023-24, a period where we had four players in the quarter-finals of the World Cup, won one Grand Swiss, and had three of those players in the Candidates. We were clearly playing the best chess during that period."Considering we were not in the best of our forms and still won silver shows how much depth and skill we have that at our best, we are going to win gold, by a big margin. But even when we are not at our best, we can still win silver. That shows how good the team is."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: USC defense, currently humiliated, has a chance to improve in Week 5
articles.summary: The Trojans' defense urgently needs to bounce back against a struggling Washington Huskies offense. It can't be more of the same
articles.body:
The USC defense's best performance this season was against Fresno State . Since then, the defense has been a liability. Against Oregon , the defense's poor play was a big reason for the embarrassing loss. This week, the Trojans face a struggling Washington offense trying to bounce back.

Here is my take on which defense will show up the most in the battle between two former Pac-12 teams in USC vs. Washington:

The Huskies are coming into this game after giving up 329 total yards to the Gophers. That is right around where this team gives up on average, at 319.2 yards per game, 14th best in the country. The Huskies' defense has given the Huskies a chance to win every game. They are not a defense that suffocates its opponents. They tend to still give up more than they should. It was not an overly dominant offensive performance by Minnesota . However, the Huskies did allow Drake Lindsey to have a day. Lindsey had 3 touchdowns and 204 yards through the air.

Jayden Maiava is a better quarterback than Lindsey, so he should still be able to be his usual productive self against the Huskies. USC's offense should not be slowed down. I expect King Miller to also have some good success against the Huskies' run defense. Who allowed Utah State's 1- 3 quarterback to run for 81 yards on them.

The Trojans ' defense should be in store for a bounce-back game. The Huskies' offense is talented, but it struggled mightily against the Gophers' defensive line. They surrendered 3 of 7 total sacks in the 4th quarter alone. The offensive line for Washington should give a great opportunity to the Trojans' pass rush to build confidence. The run game also creates no real worries for USC, as their leading rusher is quarterback Demond Williams, who has 165 total yards on the ground this season.

Demond Williams will be the key X-factor in this game. The dual-threat archetype quarterback usually tends to get the best of USC. He does not have enough talent around him and a good offensive line to help him maximize what he can do. Other teams have been able to bottle him up. I think USC has the better defense, and its defense will be a big reason why the Trojans get back on the right track with a win over Washington. I expect Luke Wafle and Jahkeem Stewart to shine and win their matchups by a wide margin.

articles.body:
The Denver Nuggets signed Cam Whitmore to a two-way contract this summer to add to their depth, and the 22-year-old swingman is reportedly turning heads at the start of the team's training camp.

During the Denver Nuggets ' Media Day, head coach David Adelman and forward Aaron Gordon took turns giving Whitmore a shoutout. Adelman and Gordon believe Whitmore will do well within their system and could help them this upcoming season.

"Big Cam. Cam's a very good player. He's big, strong, he's talented, and he's going to be a good addition. I hope that he sticks," Gordon said of Whitmore via DNVR Nuggets.

"He could play for the Broncos. I swear to God," Adelman continued. "He's got to simplify himself. He's got to drive the ball to the basket. He's got to pick up defensively. His athletic profile is incredible. There's a reason why this guy was picked high… There's a long way to go, but today's a good day for Cam. If he stays consistent, I think good things can happen to him."

"My close friend Russ ( Westbrook ), I had Russ even before it was a thought, hit Joker and ask him his thoughts on a few things," DeRozan said about how he was convinced to go to Denver. "I did my part just to get a feel for it, but every conversation I had with everybody just made me feel even more comfortable."

"My mindset is to win. To go out there, compete, be myself, go out there, help this team whatever way possible to win. Compete. At the end of the day, I love basketball. It's still basketball at the end of the day. So, me going out there, do whatever I need to win. That's all I care about," he continued.

articles.title: Los Angeles Clippers’ Brandon Ingram Opens Up on His Achilles Injury Recovery Progress
articles.summary: Brandon Ingram will miss the start of the 2026-27 NBA season, as the Los Angeles Clippers forward continues to recover from surgery on his injured heel and A...
articles.body:
Brandon Ingram will miss the start of the 2026-27 NBA season, as the Los Angeles Clippers forward continues to recover from surgery on his injured heel and Achilles.

During the Los Angeles Clippers ' Media Day on Monday, Ingram, who was part of the trade package that sent Kawhi Leonard back to the Toronto Raptors , opened up about his availability for training camp.

"My recovery has been going good. I feel good about the spot that I'm in right now, recovering from this surgery. I won't be participating in training camp much, but I'll be out there a little bit. I think it's a week-by-week thing, just trying to see when I'm going to be returning to play," Ingram told ClutchPoints' Tomer Azarly.

"I had been dealing with some pain throughout the year with the Raptors and especially coming down in crunch time. I didn't quite know what it was. Near the end of the season, we figured out what it was. We thought surgery was the best thing to do," he added.

Los Angeles Clippers News: Brandon Ingram 's injury extent explained by team president

Los Angeles Clippers interim president of basketball operations Trent Redden recently revealed that team doctors discovered and addressed Brandon Ingram's previously undisclosed Achilles injury while undergoing heel surgery last May.

"The surgery that you guys know about, he missed the end of the series with the Raptors. He had surgery on that right heel. We also found a partially torn Achilles during that time. Partially torn is much different than fully torn, so not as long. About six months less on the rehab schedule," Redden said.

"But it wasn't until we got our hands on him here that we started to see where he was at with his progression. He won't be ready for the start of the season, and we'll re-evaluate when we get there," he added. "It was part of the surgery. It was all-in-one surgery."

Ingram's injury is a bummer for the Los Angeles Clippers, as the two-time All-Star is fresh from his healthiest campaign since his rookie year. He averaged 21.5 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 3.7 assists on 47.7 percent shooting from the field across 77 regular-season appearances in 2025-26.

articles.title: Is the Marvin Harrison Jr. situation a WR, QB or scheme issue?
articles.summary: Marvin Harrison Jr. is fifth on the Cardinals in targets. How is this possible?
articles.body:
Of all the things that have been going less than well for the Arizona Cardinals , the biggest story as been the lack of production and usage for receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. Through three games, he has been targeted just nine times and has four receptions for 73 yards.

He is fifth on the team in targets, trailing the following players:

Harrison definitely should be in the top three, but what is the problem?

Is it a Harrison problem, a QB problem or a scheme problem?

One could certainly say that part of the problem is Harrison. There are clips going around where he seems to be running at half speed, just going through the motions. And that certainly is a factor, and it happens to a lot of receiver when they know they aren't getting the ball.

One could say it is a quarterback issue, as Jacoby Brissett isn't looking his way. In four healthy games with Brissett in 2025, Harrison was targeted six, 10, 12 and seven times. Brissett is not taking shots down the field. He is averaging only 5.6 yards per pass, which is not good.

However, it likely is more of a scheme issue. Head coach Mike LaFleur appears disinterested in getting Harrison involved easily early in the game. When asked about it earlier this season, he referred to McBride and Bourne rather than saying that he could find ways to get him going. That answer is telling. He isn't interested in using Harrison creatively to get him targets. He isn't a priority.

With 65 of the Cardinals' 113 (57.5%) pass attempts directed at McBride and Wilson and another 17% are dumpoffs to running backs, schematically the offense wants Harrison to do one thing — go down the field. And if there isn't time to get the ball down to him, what can anyone do? Brissett has been checking down successfully, but the lack of explosive plays is obvious.

Whatever the reason, Harrison is being wasted. There is plenty of blame to go around. But there is time to fix things.

articles.title: Why was Aaron Judge AWOL during Yankees’ introductions? What we know
articles.summary: Yankees captain Aaron Judge was left of the Wild Card Series roster and remains on the injured list with a Grade 2 right calf strain.
articles.body:
NEW YORK — Yankees fans broke into a loud cheer when they heard Giancarlo Stanton 's name during Tuesday night's player introductions as they watched the slugger pop out of the first base dugout and jog to the first base foul line.

One Yankees player was missing when Yankee Stadium PA announcer Paul Ogden announced the non-starters, injured players and taxi squad.

Where was Aaron Judge before the start of the Yankees' 9-0 Game 1 rout of the Red Sox ?

The non-starters were presented in numerical order, so first up was No. 12 Trent Grisham , who went from the IL to a backup center fielder role. Next was No. 13 Jazz Chisholm , who was on the bench with Anthony Volpe at second base.

Judge, who was unsuccessful in lobbying the Yankees to cut short his IL stint, should have been announced last.

No. 99's reception likely would have rivaled the loudest of the night — Game 1 starting pitcher Cam Schlittler 's — had he been introduced

One Yankees player told NJ.com after the game that he didn't realize Judge was absent.

Whatever the reason, Judge joined his teammates in the dugout for the game. On a chilly fall night, he wore a hoodie while watching the game from the dugout rail.

After the Yankees won, Judge was out on the field shaking hands and smiling with teammates.

Judge has made a lot of progress rehabbing his strained right calf in the last week, but the Yankees had no choice but to keep him off their 26-man roster.

Judge did not hit a ball out of the infield in four live BP at-bats during Monday's workout day, and he hasn't been cleared to run the bases.

"I wanted to see what he had," manager Aaron Boone said. "I was encouraged by what I saw, encouraged the fact that he's back and doing those kind of things and checked the necessary boxes he needed to with the trainers and the strength and conditioning to be in a position to do that."

If the Yankees finish off the Red Sox in Game 2 on Wednesday or Game 3 on Thursday, Judge will likely push harder to return for the next series. If the Yankees advance, they'll play a best-of-five AL Division Series against the Rays .

If the Yankees advance, Game 1 of the Division Series would be Saturday at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida.

The Yankees still don't have a good idea whether Judge will be ready.

"Hopefully, these next several days for him are beneficial and he continues to move the needle," Boone said.
