articles.title: Sean McVay loves Rams' resiliency amid frustrating 1-2 start
articles.summary: Sean McVay shared a message after the Rams' 1-2 start, praising the team's resiliency amid the adversity they've faced.
articles.body:
With two losses in the first three games of the season, the Los Angeles Rams have not gotten off to a hot start. At one point in the offseason, portions of the media were ready to crown them as the NFL's champions. Now, they're multiple games out of first place in the NFC West.

After a heartbreaking loss to the Denver Broncos , head coach Sean McVay and company are looking to rally with a win against the Philadelphia Eagles this week. Asked about channeling his feelings from the loss into this week's work, McVay praised his players for how they've endured the issues of the early season, saying he loves the resiliency of the Rams.

"I think you [have to] understand that tough times don't last, tough people do," said McVay. "The only real growth occurs through some of these adverse moments and you certainly don't want it. I know this, we've talked a lot about it, and this is when you get a chance to lean in. I love the resiliency of this group. I like what I've seen so far. We certainly have gotten tested and had a bunch of different unique things thrown at us in these first few weeks.

"There are a bunch of different things, but all of it represents growth opportunities. I'm interested to just see how we move forward and who we become in the midst of this journey."

That was put on display last week when multiple players stepped up due to injury issues. Josh Wallace overcame a slow start while replacing Jaylen Watson , coming away with an interception. He also nearly had another that could've ended the game, if not for a controversial defensive pass interference penalty.

Both Terrance Ferguson and Colby Parkinson battled through injury, while Davante Adams and Tyler Higbee turned back the clock on their careers.

All in all, the Rams have no quit in them as they look to get back to .500 on the season.

articles.title: El drama de Robinson Meza, en coma tras grave accidente de BMX en Francia: su familia pide ayuda
articles.standfirst: El deportista Robinson Meza lucha por su vida en Francia tras un grave accidente
articles.summary: El deportista Robinson Meza lucha por su vida en Francia tras un grave accidente
articles.body: Lo que debía ser una jornada clave en la preparación deportiva de Robinson Meza terminó convirtiéndose en una amarga pesadilla. Más conocido entre la comunidad del ciclismo extremo como ‘Robin’, el talentoso ciclista antioqueño de BMX Freestyle se encuentra internado en la Unidad de Cuidados Intensivos (UCI) de un centro médico en Francia, tras sufrir un impactante accidente mientras entrenaba. Meza, considerado uno de los exponentes más destacados de esta disciplina en Sudamérica y habitual competidor en eventos internacionales de la Unión Ciclista Internacional y Copas del Mundo, sufrió un choque múltiple en la pista con otros dos deportistas. A pesar de llevar puestos todos sus elementos de protección y el casco de seguridad, la fuerza del impacto le provocó la pérdida inmediata del conocimiento, además de múltiples fracturas en extremidades (brazos y piernas) y severas lesiones craneales. Tras el accidente, sus propios compañeros de circuito reaccionaron con rapidez para trasladarlo a un hospital cercano, donde fue ingresado en estado de coma e inducido a cuidados intensivos debido a la gravedad de los traumatismos. "Es muy abrumador todo lo que está pasando; por fortuna, Robin está mejorando. Debemos mantenernos fuertes y unidos para ayudar a estas dos grandes personas y sus familias", declaró Jefferson Calderón, allegado al deportista. Ante la emergencia, el gremio del ciclismo y del BMX en Colombia activó una campaña de apoyo bajo el lema "Juntos por Robin Meza" a través de la plataforma de recaudación Vaki. La iniciativa busca cubrir los elevados costos de la atención médica internacional, estimados de forma preliminar en más de 4.500 euros, así como logística de estadía y desplazamientos. Desde Colombia, la principal preocupación gira en torno a Débora Montoya, madre de Robinson, quien adelanta los trámites requeridos ante el consulado francés para poder viajar de urgencia y estar al frente de la recuperación de su hijo. Gracias a la solidaridad de la comunidad deportiva y allegados, la campaña de recolección de fondos ha tenido una respuesta favorable, acercándose a la meta necesaria para financiar los tiquetes aéreos, seguros de viaje y los gastos básicos de mantenimiento durante su estadía en suelo europeo. Robinson Meza forma parte de la camada de atletas que impulsaron el crecimiento del BMX Freestyle en Colombia, rama que tras su debut olímpico en Tokio 2020 vive un gran auge en la región. El deportista enfoca sus esfuerzos deportivos con miras a lograr un cupo en las justas olímpicas de Los Ángeles 2028, meta que hoy queda temporalmente en pausa mientras la comunidad ciclista del país hace fuerza por su pronta y completa recuperación.

articles.title: 13 of the Wildest Athlete Houses
articles.summary: The paydays for the world's best athletes keep getting bigger. The same goes for their real estate portfolios.
articles.body:
The paydays for the world's best athletes keep getting bigger. The same goes for their real estate portfolios.

With multi-million-dollar contracts, huge endorsement deals and more, sports stars boast some of the world's most stunning and elaborate homes. Not all megamansions are created equal, though.

While most of us can only ever dream of living in any of these places, there's no price tag on a little lighthearted judgment. With that in mind, take a look at some of the wildest athlete homes to date.

Ronaldo's real estate portfolio is among the most extensive in the sports world . He has properties spread across Portugal, Spain, Italy, the Middle East and more.

The crown jewel might be his estimated £30 million home in Quinta da Marinha on Portugal's Cascais coast. The property was under construction for more than three years, and Ronaldo and his family reportedly plan to settle there after his retirement, according to Phil Cardy of the Mirror .

Given its desirable location and unique customizations, it is one of the most expensive private homes in the country.

The mansion includes plenty of personal touches and quirks, like a giant glass swimming pool with an underwater walkway so guests can see who is swimming above. The property includes two swimming pools (one indoor and one outdoor), a gym, a spa, a screening room and extensive landscaped gardens.

Can you imagine owning a home so elaborate that it earned a nickname? Derek Jeter's famous waterfront mansion, nicknamed "St. Jetersburg," was actually located in Tampa, not St. Petersburg, but close enough.

Jeter owned the 20,000-plus-square-foot mega-mansion when he was playing for the New York Yankees, as it was conveniently located near their spring training facilities. The seven-bedroom, eight-full-bathroom home included an elaborate spa, multiple yacht decks, and two separate three-car garages.

It has since been torn down, but not before Jeter rented it to Tom Brady when he started playing for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Just like we'll always look back on Jeter's career as larger than life, we'll remember St. Jetersburg in all its glory.

Aussie golf legend Greg Norman decided to downsize as he hit his 70s, but he and his family lived in an extravagant estate named Tranquility in Jupiter, Florida, for nearly 30 years.

Sold in 2021 for $55.1 million, the 8.3-acre compound is truly a sight to behold. It had more than 30,000 square feet of living space, according to Coldwell Banker , and boasted 10 bedrooms, 12 bathrooms and six half-bathrooms.

The estate had a dock that could accommodate a 150-foot yacht, along with a U.S. Open-sized tennis court, per Janice O'Leary of Yahoo.

NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 4 🏈

This list wouldn't be complete without a nod to Tiger Woods' oceanside mansion on Jupiter Island. Reportedly worth around $54 million , the property is where Woods has spent most of his time since it was completed in 2011.

Woods' mansion sits on several acres and features its own golf course, basketball court, tennis courts, swimming pools and a state-of-the-art gym. There are gorgeous ocean views and living areas, but the fitness and training facilities truly set Woods' estate apart.

Known for his love of privacy—which is also the name of his yacht —Woods designed this place so he can stay on top of his golf game and fitness regimen without ever leaving the house.

Oh, and that yacht? It's docked on the private beach that is part of the property.

Woods' place is every introverted athlete's dream.

Floyd Mayweather's primary residence is a sprawling $10 million compound in the exclusive Queensridge community of Las Vegas. The 22,000-square-foot compound features a main house, two guest houses, 11 bedrooms, 14 bathrooms, a 1.41-acre vineyard and, of course, a 20-car subterranean garage.

Perhaps the most distinct external feature of the compound is the gorgeous, oh-so-Vegas fountain.

This isn't even the most expensive mansion Mayweather has purchased. His properties in Beverly Hills and Florida cost more. But there's something so charming, elaborate and distinctly Vegas about this one.

You know the man known for his many endorsement deals—along with his Hall of Fame NBA career, of course—has lived in some epic places. Shaquille O'Neal's former 31,000-square-foot Orlando mansion is the most elaborate.

The 12-bedroom lakeside home is in the exclusive Isleworth Community, a 600-acre golf-club community bordering a lake. There are personalized Shaq touches all over it, like a 6,000-square-foot indoor basketball court, a 17-car garage, a 95-foot-long pool, and Superman branding throughout.

Serena Williams' 14,500-square-foot waterfront Florida home is modern with a personal flair. Serena designed it with help from none other than her sister, Venus.

In an interview with Architectural Digest , Williams said they transformed the house from Spanish-style to a more contemporary feel.

"I was moving away from Venus for the first time in my life, so I wanted it to be really meaningful," she said. "You have to know your lane. I'm really good at playing tennis; I'm not as good at interiors. But I was able to learn through just watching Venus."

The modern art and personal touches make the place feel less like a property and more like a home. Unlike most athletes on this list, Serena intentionally opted for no tennis court to keep work and home life separate. Instead, the home features a private trophy room for her awards, a gym, a sauna, and a princess-themed room for her daughter, Olympia.

For those seeking that distinct Tuscan style as opposed to a more modern look, Joe Montana's former home is the pinnacle.

The Tuscan-style villa spans 500 acres of California's Napa Valley wine country. Of course there's a wine cellar. It can hold 3,500 bottles, and it also holds olive oil sourced from the estate's own olive trees, according to Amy Graff of SF Gate.

We could go on about the features of the home, like a professional equestrian center, tons of outdoor sports amenities and Napa Valley views. Still, the stunning architecture featuring European antiques, imported 16th-century iron gates and antique marble floors and attention to Tuscan-style detail steal the show.

This Miami stunner, which Dwyane Wade and Gabrielle Union sold in 2021 for $22 million , is more like a personal resort.

Spanning 12,000 square feet, the six-bedroom property features a private basketball court, a chef's kitchen, a wine room, and a state-of-the-art theater.

According to Claudine Zap of Realtor.com, the home also has a "private dock, a pool, a gazebo with a bar, an outdoor kitchen and a Miami Heat-themed basketball court."

These recent Yankees legends have a keen eye for real estate. A-Rod's home in Coral Gables, Florida, has earned praise from experts like Architectural Digest for good reason.

The mid-century modern property spans 11,877 square feet and features all of the lavish amenities we've come to expect out of athlete homes like a basketball court. But Rodriguez's extensive art collection, including some Andy Warhols, steals the show.

What does a castle fit for a King look like?

In 2020, LeBron James took a nearly $37 million Beverly Hills mansion off the market, a home that has been home to several Hollywood stars over the years. He still has the Akron mansion that he bought at 18, among other residences, but his latest is a sight to see.

The main house spans nearly 16,000 square feet across two stories, per Charlie Lankston of Realtor.com, and James has done significant work to update it with modern luxuries, including a home theatre. There's no bowling alley like he has in his Akron place, but when in Hollywood, you opt for the home theatre.

Before James got to work on his renovations, the grounds boasted a tennis court, a pool house and two guest houses. And of course, there's a customized basketball court.

Maybe instead of asking ourselves who's the GOAT on the court, we can ask ourselves who has the best real estate portfolio between Michael Jordan and LeBron James.

Jordan may no longer reside in his famous Chicago mansion, but his fingerprints are all over it.

The nine-bedroom, 15-bathroom estate features an entertainment area, a state-of-the-art gym, a putting green and, of course, a full size indoor basketball court.

Jordan famously struggled to sell the place due to the high asking price and the larger-than-life feel of it all, but that doesn't mean it isn't an amazing property. Maybe he should've considered turning it into a museum.

Back in 2020, Steph Curry bought a three-story Silicon Valley mansion for $30 million in the most expensive zip code in the U.S., according to Kasia Pawlowska of SF Gate.

The modern-style home is sleek as can be, with stucco and glass everywhere you look. The property offers more than 17,000 square feet of living space, including seven bedrooms and eight-and-a-half bathrooms, plus a guest house and a walnut orchard.

The Currys sold the house earlier this year for $29 million, which sparked debate about Steph's future in the Bay Area. But he was likely just playing the real estate game since he recently signed an extension with the Warriors.

articles.title: China extends 52-year unbeaten record as Asian Games organisers apologise
articles.summary: Chinese divers were unstoppable as the country’s sizeable overall tally of gold medals swelled to 150.
articles.body:
China’s divers extended their remarkable Asian Games unbeaten record stretching back to 1974 as a top Japanese official apologised for “inconveniences” that have dogged the continent’s premier sporting event.

Chinese divers were unstoppable once more on Wednesday as the country’s sizeable overall tally of gold medals swelled to 150 with four days left.

Hosts Japan are a distant second with 50 golds, ahead of South Korea with 24.

Chen Yiwen and Lian Junjie each won gold in the final two diving events to give China a 14th consecutive clean sweep in the sport.

China has won every diving gold medal since their first Asian Games appearance 52 years ago.

“Girls are every bit as capable as boys. We are pushing ourselves to perform more difficult dives, too,” said Chen, a double Paris Olympics champion.

“We do not train any less than the boys,” she added.

In tennis, the Philippines’ Alexandra Eala stormed into the semifinals, cheered on by fans who had come from far and wide to see their hero in action.

The world number 18 and favourite for women’s singles gold had to work hard early on to beat Taiwan’s England-born Joanna Garland 7-5, 6-0 in her second outing in Nagoya.

The winner of the tournament qualifies for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

“Representing my country and playing these types of games, SEA Games, Asian Games and hopefully the Olympics, they’re very close to my heart and a big part of my dreams,” said Eala.

She plays China’s Wang Xiyu, ranked 85, next.

Taiwan boxer Lin Yu-ting, the Olympic champion who found herself embroiled in a major gender row at Paris 2024, is guaranteed at least a silver medal.

Lin outclassed Sitora Turdibekova of Uzbekistan 5-0 in the women’s 60kg class to surge into the final, putting her one win from a second Asian Games gold.

The 30-year-old thanked the medical team afterwards for treating the cut to her nose she suffered in the quarterfinals.

In football, South Korea scored an 82nd-minute winner in a 2-1 victory over China in the men’s semifinals.

They will face Japan for gold after the hosts pulled through against Uzbekistan 9-8 on penalties, the game having ended 1-1 after 120 minutes.

Meanwhile, on Wednesday Nagoya’s mayor apologised to athletes for “inconveniences” at the games following a string of complaints.

The event has been marred by problems including a shortage of beds and issues with transport.

There are more than 17,000 athletes and officials, more than the Olympics, and countries have accused local organisers of mismanagement.

“We must offer our apologies to the athletes and others affected by these inconveniences,” said Mayor Ichiro Hirosawa, who is also acting chairman of the local organising committee.

“We must sincerely reflect on the mishandling that occurred,” he added.

Unlike past games, there is no athletes’ village, with participants instead sleeping in temporary wooden units, on a cruise ship and in hotels to save money.

articles.title: Arizona State places men's hockey coach Greg Powers on administrative leave
articles.summary: Matthew Mayich remains hospitalized and in a coma a month after collapsing during an outdoor team workout.
articles.body:
Arizona State men's hockey head coach Greg Powers has been placed on administrative leave in the wake of an outdoor workout that left sophomore Matthew Mayich on life support and in a coma in August.

"Our focus continues to be on Matthew and his family, and on our student-athletes to make sure they have the support they need during this time and as the season begins," said Arizona State athletic director Graham Rossini in a statement. "We have continued to collect as much information as possible. After thorough and careful deliberation, I believe this is the best move to provide stability for the hockey program."

The decision comes days after players and Mayich's parents called for Powers to be placed on leave. Seven Sun Devils players wrote a 26-page letter to Arizona State president Michael Crow on Monday that was obtained by The Athletic . They wrote the letter anonymously through an attorney, as they said they fear retaliation from Powers.

Mayich was participating in a workout with the team on Aug. 20 when he collapsed and later fell into a coma. The workout was described as "grueling" and run by an ex-U.S. Army Green Beret.

The players disputed several findings from the university's initial review of the Aug. 20 workout that resulted in Mayich's collapse, including that he did not receive water and was provided inadequate medical care after collapsing. A water break was given around 40 minutes into the 75-minute workout, but it lasted just seconds, according to the players. Only about eight players actually received water, they said, as they were the first who had just finished a bear-crawl drill moments before.

At one point, they said, the Green Beret admitted to forgetting that players needed water and said that he didn't drink water during combat.

Mayich, they said, showed obvious signs of distress early in the workout. They said he became disoriented during the bear crawl and could not carry a teammate during a buddy-carry exercise. At one point, they said, he leaned on another teammate in order to stand up while a drill was being explained to them.

Once Mayich collapsed, they said, he remained in direct sunlight for several minutes. Unlike what Arizona State said in its report, which stated Mayich remained on the ground, players said that he twice sat upright, once on the field and later when he was carried into the shade by teammates. The only cooling mechanisms there, they said, were small towels from a cooler, water from squirt bottles and water sprayed from a garden hose.

They also said the team did not properly acclimate players, including those from colder locations — Mayich is from Ontario — to the Arizona heat. The only outdoor workouts they did before Aug. 20, the players said, were roughly 15 minutes long.

"The concerns raised by student-athletes deserve to be heard and thoroughly reviewed," read a statement from the National Collegiate Hockey Conference. "We will not prejudge the findings of that review. Hockey matters deeply to our conference, but the well-being of our student-athletes matters more."

Mayich, a 2023 sixth-round draft pick by the St. Louis Blues , transferred to Arizona State from Clarkson University this past summer and had previously played in the Ontario Hockey League. His lawyer said earlier this month that he has "zero chance of recovery."

Powers was asked about the incident repeatedly last week, but refused to talk about it other than saying it's been "a difficult time" for the program. Powers, the players alleged, downplayed Mayich's condition initially and told them he needed only an IV after suffering "just a little heat stroke." Powers also told them that they were "closer to making the Frozen Four because of the workout and Matthew having pushed himself to the maximum." The next day, they said, Powers told them that he had received "good news" and Mayich would be fine.

Powers has been head coach of the program since 2010 and later he led the team from the club level to an NCAA Division I program in 2015. He signed a five-year extension last November.

The Sun Devils open their season Friday, and assistant Mike Corbett will assume coaching duties while Powers is away from the team. An interim head coach will reportedly be named soon, according to the Grand Forks Herald's Brad Elliott Schlossman .

articles.title: Super League Grand Final: Sam Burgess and Daryl Powell know weight of expectation as Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity make history
articles.summary: Sam Burgess and Daryl Powell have the same task in the Grand Final and that is to win the trophy for the first time for their clubs; watch Warrington Wolves take on Wakefield Trinity in the Super League Grand Final on Saturday October 3, live on Sky Sports from 5pm
articles.body:
Hull KR beat Wigan Warriors, who are one of the big clubs that have won the Grand Final over and over.

For Warrington and Wakefield, the task is very different - neither have won this trophy and history is guaranteed.

Of course, that adds an extra layer of pressure as Sam Burgess and Daryl Powell look to do something that their respective town and city have dreamt of since their introduction to Super League.

For Burgess, the moment has many similarities to the one he experienced as a player with South Sydney Rabbitohs when they ended their 43-year wait for the big trophy in 2014. Burgess was player of the match and iconic images remain of him playing with a fractured cheekbone.

With Warrington, he would end a 71-year drought and he admits it is a major motivator.

"I'd be lying if I said I wasn't very interested in trying to break the drought when I first took the job," Burgess said.

"There's a lot of similarities between Warrington and South Sydney Rabbitohs.

"It's not been won here for 71 years, I'm aware of that. It's exciting, but as a player at Souths, we got to the prelims in 2012 and 2013 before we won it in 2014.

"I felt like all that drought talk, weight of expectation, it was heavy.

"But it's not heavy on us, because we've kept it that way. It's more about this new group and creating our own history rather than being weighed down by the past."

Powell has taken Wakefield on an incredible journey from being in the Championship for the 2024 season, returning in 2025, and now making it all the way to the Grand Final.

Not only that, they did it in some style with a 33-6 victory over Wigan in the semi-final. Wigan were the clear favourites having already picked up a domestic double in 2026.

Now, it is for Powell to make even more history with the biggest win in Wakefield's existence but he is more focused on playing good rugby and from that, the result will follow.

He does concede, though, that it would be the cherry on top of what has been a remarkable narrative.

"These boys are impeccable human beings, I think. We're in a great place, we're tuned in," Powell said.

"I think the players, from what I've seen so far, are pretty relaxed, pretty calm. There's going to be some nerves. I think getting all of our prep right will be important, but I feel like we've done a massive amount of preparation over the last seven or eight weeks, where we've been playing against all the best teams.

"I try not to think about it, because I'd ask the players not to think about winning the game, I would ask the players to just be in the game, to play the game.

"That never helps you, all it can do is create anxiety and I don't see any point in that. Clearly it would be unbelievable if we win the game.

"We're on a great journey, the club's on a great journey, and this is the next step, this is a step for us into a great arena with an opportunity to do something unbelievably special.

"It'll be a phenomenal story, and I think we're good enough to do it. It's all about Saturday and the boys just doing what they do best and making sure that we play the game we want to play.

"If we get that right, the result will take care of itself."

How to watch the Super League Grand Final

The Super League Grand Final takes place at Old Trafford on Saturday October 3, live on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports+ .

The match will kick-off at 6pm, with coverage on Sky Sports from 5pm.

articles.title: Ronaldo leaves Portugal camp amid reports of rift with coach Jorge Jesus
articles.summary: Ronaldo did not play in Portugal’s 2-1 win over Norway ‌on Sunday and will now miss the game against Denmark.
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo confirmed ⁠on ⁠Wednesday that he had left Portugal’s training camp after a ⁠turbulent few hours in Copenhagen, amid reports of ⁠a dispute with coach Jorge Jesus, on the eve of their Nations League match against Denmark .

“Following the national team manager’s press conference, and after a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I ⁠have decided to leave ⁠the national team’s training camp,” Ronaldo wrote on Instagram, adding that ⁠he would tell Portuguese fans “the truth ⁠about the reasons ⁠behind my departure” in due course.

The Portugal squad later arrived at their ‌hotel without Ronaldo and without Jesus, with the whereabouts ‌of ‌both still unknown.

Earlier on Wednesday, Jesus denied Ronaldo had refused to train as the Portuguese Football ⁠Federation (FPF) confirmed the ⁠forward did not take part in the team’s final session before Thursday’s game.

Portuguese newspaper A Bola posted a video that ⁠appeared to show Ronaldo leaving Copenhagen’s Parken Stadium in a FPF vehicle. A Bola reported that Ronaldo left shortly after Jesus had said the 41-year-old would take part in the session.

Spanish sports media ⁠outlet Marca reported that Ronaldo intended to board a private flight to Madrid in the coming hours.

Ronaldo did not play in Portugal’s 2-1 win over Norway ‌on Sunday after Jesus told him he would come off the bench but ultimately decided against bringing him on.

He then worked in the gym rather than training with the rest of the squad on Monday and Tuesday, despite not being injured.

Speaking at a news conference before Wednesday’s session, Jesus told reporters not to manufacture a controversy and said it was normal for Ronaldo to miss team training in the days after a ⁠match.

“He didn’t refuse. He’s going to train today,” said Jesus.

“It’s the ⁠fourth day, so he’s going to train. And he didn’t refuse to train. It’s impossible. Do you believe that? Not Cris.”

Jesus said there had been no incident, although he confirmed speaking to Ronaldo about the situation.

“They forced ⁠me to talk to Cris about an issue that didn’t exist. There was nothing to talk about,” said Jesus.

“He said, ‘I’m here for ⁠you to decide. If you want me to play, ⁠I’ll play. If you want me to go to the stands, I’ll go.'”

FPF President Pedro Proenca travelled to Copenhagen on Tuesday.

A Bola reported that Proenca had changed his plans and gone to Denmark ‌to meet Jesus and Ronaldo before Portugal’s Nations League match there on Thursday.

Ronaldo is Portugal’s record goalscorer with 146 goals and their most-capped player with 234 appearances. Ronaldo told a ‌news ‌conference last week that the media had been trying to “kill” him for years, and said that he could leave “today” if the manager did not want him in the squad.

articles.title: Klint vs Spags and Leonard vs Reid winner leads the AFC West
articles.summary: With Week 4 upcoming, coaching has made all the difference to the Raiders. Against the Chiefs, it has to be at its best.
articles.body:
For the last 13 years, the Raiders have been tormented by the offense and play calling of Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid. Reid and the Chiefs have been to the Super Bowl five times, winning three. Making them the team of the late 2o-teens and early 2020's. Additionally, winning nine straight division crowns.

Reid has been game-planning his players for career days for nearly 30 years. We've seen shovel passes, ring around the rosie, fly sweeps and screens. All kinds of disrespectful plays that show a lack of regard for the rules of defenses. He's had to do some of his best work lately with less talented players and aging stars on the roster. This week, Reid will need to be at his very best if he hopes to avoid getting shut out in the clutch, like Kellen Moore did on Sunday.

Rob Leonard has done amazing things in a short amount of time for the Raiders defense. He's devised ways to engineer turnovers, attack offenses with proper timing and out-coach opposing offenses. Designing schemes to place players in positions to do what they do best when called on. Through three games, his defense has yet to surrender a fourth-quarter point, often making offenses look foolish.

The mighty Raiders defense is ranked first in pressure rate (50%), turnovers (9), forced fumbles (10) and interceptions (4). They are tied for fourth with 10 sacks, ranked fifth with 41 total pressures all while blitzing only 25% of pass plays. Leonard's unit is playing team defense; communicating, doing things the Raiders haven't seen in decades, if ever.

Steve Spagnuolo, Chiefs defensive coordinator, has been a premier defensive mind with his exotic blitz packages for decades. He has developed elite-level talents and his defenses have, in fact, won championships in multiple locations. For the seven years he has coordinated defense in Kansas City , he has left Raiders' offenses seeing red.

Screwing up pre-snap reads with disguised alignments, soft-shoeing receivers (playing man coverage at zone depths), and bringing blitzes from the second and third levels. These were just a few of the many tricks used to completely ground opposing passing games. Rushing attacks have been rendered stationary with run blitzes and the fundamentals he coaches up. and and too much laughing at the Raiders futility. That stops this year.

Klint Kubiak, the Raiders head coach and play caller, isn't accepting flowers after three weeks. Winning isn't foreign to Kubiak; last season he and the Seattle Seahawks offense won the Super Bowl with Sam Darnold under center. Kubiak has proven to be one heck of a play caller and an even better play designer. His attention to detail, game plan preparation and in-game adjustments have the Raiders offense ranked seventh in scoring offense and EPA per play.

Kubiak has been getting it done the old-fashioned way, with multiple tight end sets, a fullback and a run-heavy approach. Impressively, he is getting production from practice squad players in the red zone, stacking up 29.3 points per game and looking unbeatable with maximum efficiency. Doing it with the steely reserve of someone who has been there before. When adversity struck in a hostile environment, down 11 points, his team proceeded to score 19 straight points through the end of the third quarter until it was all over.

articles.title: Baltimore Ravens: Add Center With 61 Starts to the Squad

articles.body:
As previously discussed on Gridiron Heroics, the Baltimore Ravens needed to address the center position after placing starter Jovaughn Gwyn (fractured fibula) and backup Ethan Pocic (knee) on injured reserve. Gwyn is expected to miss at least two to three months, maybe longer, while Pocic currently has no timetable for return. As a result, first-round pick Olaivavega Ioane is a strong candidate to take over as the starting center and will get starting reps there in practice this week.

To make matters worse, the Ravens have no centers on either the active roster or the practice squad. The team worked out multiple interior offensive linemen on Tuesday, including Graham Glasgow . The 34-year-old Glasgow served as the Lions' center last season, but his struggles led to his release in March.

The Baltimore Ravens add a center with 61 starts to the squad

On X, the Ravens announced that they have signed Andre James and guard Kyle Hergel to the practice squad. The 29-year-old James brings ample experience, having started 61 regular-season and one playoff game, primarily at center. Unfortunately, things have not panned out for the former Raiders starter, and he has bounced around with two teams since being released in 2024.

Both players can be elevated to the game-day roster three times without penalty; otherwise, a fourth elevation would require a promotion to the active roster.

The Chargers signed Andre James to a one-year deal last March. James served as the team's backup center and was limited to one start and 84 offensive snaps, the lowest total since 2020. The Titans signed him to a one-year deal in June, but he suffered an undisclosed injury, resulting in Tennessee placing him on injured reserve in late August. James was released with an injuy settlement in early September and remained unsigned through the first three weeks of the season.

articles.title: ‘I Did Sell It’: Broncos WR Admits Flopping on Game-Changing Call vs. Rams
articles.summary: "I did sell it." Broncos WR Pat Bryant admits to flopping on a crucial pass interference call that helped Denver secure a comeback win over the Rams. The pos...
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams fans were outraged after the Denver Broncos pulled out a come-from-behind 30-26 win on Sunday, and not just because the Rams blew a 16-point halftime lead.

What appeared to be a game-sealing interception by Josh Wallace with just over one minute left in the game was instead ruled pass interference, giving the Broncos a fresh set of downs.

They ultimately turned that penalty into points with quarterback Bo Nix 's touchdown run with 47 seconds left.

The Broncos receiver involved in that interception-turned-penalty, though, appears to have admitted he played up the situation to try to get the refs involved.

Speaking with Romi Bean of CBS Sports Colorado , Broncos wide receiver Pat Bryant initially laughed when asked point-blank if it was indeed pass interference.

"It was a little pass interference," he replied. "I did sell it just enough, you know what I'm saying, to get the flag, but he did give me a little nudge that I felt, and I felt like I couldn't get the ball. So, it was either the ball or the call, and we ended up getting the call."

Bryant then agreed with Bean that Wallace "definitely gave me a shove."

He also expounded upon Bean's question if NFL players were learning "the art of the flop" like soccer and basketball players have.

"Oh yeah, of course," he responded while a clip of the play is shown. "Boom, you see it here. Once they give you that push, it's either illegal contact or pass interference. I know that's the biggest thing going across social media right now. I can't even open my social media without seeing the video, but it's something a lot of people do in this league, so I kind of use it to my advantage."

If the comments were any indication, Bryant's answers will only stir up more controversy, not settle the matter.

And that makes sense, as the call clearly could have gone either way.

Bryant admitting that he chose trying to get the call over trying to catch the ball is inflaming the emotions of those Rams fans who already thought they'd been cheated.

It's too late to change the result, though, and the Rams now sit at 1-2 amid a tough start to what was supposed to be a special season .

If the Rams can take down the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, though, it's likely to feel like everything is back on track.

articles.title: Joe Mazzulla on how Boston Celtics will deal with a stronger NBA Eastern Conference
articles.summary: "I think the league is really good. I think the league is as balanced as it's ever been," said Mazzulla.
articles.body:
For many years now, the NBA's Western Conference has been the dominant of the two, with the Eastern Conference the junior partner in the Association in terms of the strength of the ball clubs that comprise it. But this season, even though consensus has the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder as the two best teams in the league, it is the East that is the stronger conference from teams Nos. 1 to 15.

And that is not lost on Boston Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla, who spoke about how this surge in difficulty may impact the Celtics campaign ahead after a training camp practice on Wednesday (Sep. 30) morning. "For us, it felt like regular season has always meant the same amount," said Mazzulla via CLNS Media. "I think … one of the strengths of the guys on the roster and the locker room is there's very few regular season games that I don't feel that … we take them seriously."

"So I expect that regardless of … the strength of the conference or not," he added. "At the same time, it is a really deep conference, and I think the league is really good. I think the league is as balanced as it's ever been."

"Going roster for roster, there's a ton of great teams out there," said Mazzulla. "There's a ton of different matchups that could give teams problems on any given night, and … with the rule changes, you're going to expect more of that."

"And so we were talking to the team about that yesterday. When the schedule comes out, based on how the league had been in the past, you could look at 10 or so games, and be like 'Okay, that's one that we're going to get', whereas I think where the rosters are and the way the league is now, there's maybe zero of those."

"I think it makes the competition better," said the Celtics coach. "I think it forces us to get better and better every game."

articles.title: Malachi Moreno believes Ousmane N’Diaye has All-American potential
articles.summary: Moreno believes N’Diaye will surprise a lot of people this season.
articles.body:
When Ousmane N'Diaye committed to Kentucky on April 24, most fans would have been lying if they said they had heard of him.

Now, with the season less than a month away, Big Blue Nation has learned more and more about him over the offseason.

From learning he technically committed while watching the Michael Jackson movie to seeing his elite offensive skills in summer highlights, we've learned a lot more about him since he arrived in the United States from Senegal.

N'Diaye is a 7-foot, 220-pound gifted offensive weapon who can deliver some of the best highlights imaginable, given his size. Stepback threes, ball-handling, violent dunks. He's got a world of potential.

His teammate and sophomore center for Kentucky, Malachi Moreno, was asked about N'Diaye at Media Day and what he has seen from him in the last few months. His response is pretty noteworthy and should get fans excited to watch him.

"He's changed his game a ton. I think the first couple weeks were kind of getting an overall feel for what college basketball is, but ever since then, he is something else. He's shooting the ball, and I think just overall his physicality is just taking a big step forward, and he's going to surprise a lot of people. Might even be an All-American," said Moreno via Wyatt Huff .

That final line makes you take a step back and think: Maybe this guy, seen as a mystery player and a question mark, is just the one we watched in his overseas highlights, and his game may translate perfectly.

Moreno continued, saying, "I think from what I've seen on tapes, I think overseas he was kind of spread out on the floor a little bit more, not asked as much to do a lot in the paint. So I think he's kind of understanding what it is now, and now he's really starting to play. "

Overseas prospects have a wide range of outcomes: some thrive, and some struggle. Based on what Moreno shared, we may have a guy in N'Diaye who is figuring it out and will bring a lot of elite offensive moments to Kentucky this season.

Mark Pope and his staff have coached forwards on opposite ends of the skill spectrum. A guy like Andrew Carr brings a skilled offensive game and can stretch the floor, while a guy like Mouhamed Dioubate brings more physicality and a defensive/rebounding focus to his game.

Ousmane is already turning the heads of people inside the facility, so hopefully, he'll soon be turning the heads of people around the college basketball world.
